     8  public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.ConstantSheaf
     9  public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Equivalence
    10  public import Mathlib.Condensed.Basic
    11  public import Mathlib.Condensed.Light.Basic
    12  public import Mathlib.Condensed.Light.Instances
    13  /-!
    14  
    15  # Discrete-underlying adjunction
    16  
    17  Given a category `C` with sheafification with respect to the coherent topology on compact Hausdorff
    18  spaces, we define a functor `C ⥤ Condensed C` which associates to an object of `C` the
    19  corresponding "discrete" condensed object (see `Condensed.discrete`).
    20  
    21  In `Condensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj` we prove that this functor is left adjoint to the forgetful
    22  functor from `Condensed C` to `C`.
    23  
    24  We also give the variant `LightCondensed.discreteUnderlyingAdj` for light condensed objects.
    25  
    26  The file `Mathlib/Condensed/Discrete/Characterization.lean` defines a predicate `IsDiscrete` on
    27  condensed and light condensed objects, and provides several conditions on a (light) condensed
    28  set or module that characterize it as discrete.
    29  -/
    30  
    31  @[expose] public section
    32  
    33  universe u v w
    34  
    35  open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite GrothendieckTopology
    36  
    37  namespace Condensed
    38  
    39  variable (C : Type w) [Category.{u + 1} C] [HasWeakSheafify (coherentTopology CompHaus.{u}) C]
    40  
    41  /--
    42  The discrete condensed object associated to an object of `C` is the constant sheaf at that object.
    43  -/
    44  @[simps!]
    45  noncomputable def discrete : C ⥤ Condensed.{u} C := constantSheaf _ C
    46  
    47  /--
    48  The underlying object of a condensed object in `C` is the condensed object evaluated at a point.
    49  This can be viewed as a sort of forgetful functor from `Condensed C` to `C`
    50  -/
    51  @[simps!]
    52  noncomputable def underlying : Condensed.{u} C ⥤ C :=
    53    (sheafSections _ _).obj ⟨CompHaus.of PUnit.{u + 1}⟩
    54  
    55  /--
    56  Discreteness is left adjoint to the forgetful functor. When `C` is `Type*`, this is analogous to
    57  `TopCat.adj₁ : TopCat.discrete ⊣ forget TopCat`.
    58  -/
    59  noncomputable def discreteUnderlyingAdj : discrete C ⊣ underlying C :=
    60    constantSheafAdj _ _ CompHaus.isTerminalPUnit
    61  
    62  end Condensed
    63  
    64  namespace LightCondensed
    65  
    66  variable (C : Type w) [Category.{u} C] [HasSheafify (coherentTopology LightProfinite.{u}) C]
    67  
    68  /--
    69  The discrete light condensed object associated to an object of `C` is the constant sheaf at that
    70  object.
    71  -/
    72  @[simps!]
    73  noncomputable def discrete : C ⥤ LightCondensed.{u} C := constantSheaf _ C
    74  
    75  /--
    76  The underlying object of a condensed object in `C` is the light condensed object evaluated at a
    77  point. This can be viewed as a sort of forgetful functor from `LightCondensed C` to `C`
    78  -/
    79  @[simps!]
    80  noncomputable def underlying : LightCondensed.{u} C ⥤ C :=
    81    (sheafSections _ _).obj (op (LightProfinite.of PUnit))
    82  
    83  /--
    84  Discreteness is left adjoint to the forgetful functor. When `C` is `Type*`, this is analogous to
    85  `TopCat.adj₁ : TopCat.discrete ⊣ forget TopCat`.
    86  -/
    87  noncomputable def discreteUnderlyingAdj : discrete C ⊣ underlying C :=
    88    constantSheafAdj _ _ CompHausLike.isTerminalPUnit
    89  
    90  end LightCondensed
